record.title: OpenAI describes an inference-layer stop system for research model workloads
record.summary: OpenAI's November 9 post describes Control Room, a central authorization service for model inference jobs across its research infrastructure. The design assigns each workload a job ID that inference engines check before generating output; after a stop decision, later requests are denied. OpenAI reports a 35-second maximum stop interval due to authorization caching and says the service fails closed if unavailable. It reports fail-closed rollout complete for frontier research workloads and still expanding across remaining research workloads. These deployment and performance properties are first-party claims without independent operational validation in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI published a description of its Control Room workload authorization and stop system on November 9, 2026.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI says research workloads register job identifiers and inference engines check authorization before producing output; after a stop decision, further requests for that job are denied. It says the system covers research inference workloads including training and evaluation sampling and data processing.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI reports a maximum 35-second interval from receipt of a stop instruction until further progress is no longer possible, due to authorization caching. It says Control Room failure denies inference, that fail-closed rollout is complete for frontier research workloads and that rollout to remaining research workloads is continuing.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: This review did not independently verify implementation coverage, fail-closed behavior, or the stated stop bound under live or failure conditions.

evidence_gaps.description: Independent evidence for complete research workload coverage, including non-frontier workloads, was not located in this review.
The 35-second maximum and fail-closed behavior have not been independently tested under stop, cache, service outage or tampering conditions.

brief.importance_rationale: If the described inference authorization gate is deployed across research workloads, its stop path and fail-closed behavior could materially affect how a frontier lab contains safety or security risks; the deployment guarantees remain first-party claims.
limitations: The operational performance, coverage and fail-closed properties in the post are OpenAI claims, not independently verified measurements.
OpenAI says fail-closed rollout is complete for frontier research workloads but remains in progress across its other research workloads.
This record concerns research inference workloads and does not independently establish the effectiveness of external model-serving shutdown controls.
brief.summary: OpenAI's November 9 post describes Control Room, a central authorization service for model inference jobs across its research infrastructure. The design assigns each workload a job ID that inference engines check before generating output; after a stop decision, later requests are denied. OpenAI reports a 35-second maximum stop interval due to authorization caching and says the service fails closed if unavailable. It reports fail-closed rollout complete for frontier research workloads and still expanding across remaining research workloads. These deployment and performance properties are first-party claims without independent operational validation in this review.

technical.claimed_result: OpenAI says the system tracks research model workloads and can halt further model output after a stop decision, with a 35-second maximum delay and fail-closed handling of Control Room outages.
technical.demonstrated_result: OpenAI published a dated technical description of the workload-ID and inference-authorization design on November 9, 2026. No operational claim was independently tested.
technical.mechanism: Workloads register with a central service and attach the returned job ID to inference requests. Before output, inference engines ask the service whether that job remains authorized; stopped jobs receive refusal instead of model output. Authorization caching is cited as the source of a maximum 35-second stop delay.
technical.regime: OpenAI research inference infrastructure, including reinforcement-learning experiments, evaluations, high-volume sampling and data processing; rollout status differs between frontier and remaining research workloads.
technical.reproducibility: The post describes the architecture but provides no public source code, independent audit, measured test protocol or incident data in the reviewed material.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI contrasts inference-engine authorization checks with reliance on researcher-owned, changing and decentralized workload code.

brief.title: OpenAI describes an inference-layer stop system for research model workloads
brief.why_it_matters: A central inference authorization gate could reduce dependence on individual research jobs to stop model output after a safety or security intervention. The design is a material operational control claim, but its coverage and stated failure/latency guarantees remain unverified outside OpenAI's account.
